newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom interconnection charges "high" - FT.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom interconnection charges "high" - FT.

text.p: France Telecom is proposing a level of interconnection charges for rival operators which is higher than in the U.K. and Australia but at the same level as in Sweden, the Financial Times (FT) said on Wednesday.

Citing a consultation document, the FT said France Telecom was proposing a charge of 0.16 francs per minute for a local operator zone of up to 220,000 subscribers rising to 0.18 francs in so-called transit operator zones and 0.26 francs for calls outside a single operator zone.

The French Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon is currently conducting a wide consultation on the issue of interconnection charges -- the levies new operators have to pay to France Telecom for the use of its network.

The consultation will end on November 30 and the minister will issue decrees on the matter in early 1997 in order to have a price catalogue ready before the first tranche of the share listing of France Telecom, expected from April.
France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said on Monday that he wanted a level of prices that would stimulate the market and not give excessive advantages to either France Telecom or its rivals.
Philipe Glotin, chief executive of telecoms group CEGETEL, said on Tuesday that the level of interconnections charges meant "the right to die or the right to live" for France Telecom's rivals.
CEGETEL is owned by Generale des Eaux, British Telecom Plc and Mannesmann.
